subject: Quarry Labs: conditional POC top‑up and packaging options
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@quarrylabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on POC top-up/packaging options

Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to finishing a short internal review and have one procurement/ops question before we sign the POC order: if we need a small top‑up mid‑POC (we're seeing higher token usage in intent extraction), do you offer a conditional top‑up charge (pay‑as‑you‑go for overflow) or do we need to amend the timebox to add days (and associated minimums)?

Also: any concerns about moving from the hosted SKU to dedicated briefly for a 48‑hour stress test? We want predictable performance for a short window without overcommitting long term.

Appreciate a short note on options and a one‑pager we can share with procurement.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Product Operations, Quarry Labs
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@quarrylabs.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC top-up/packaging options

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we support both approaches, and the right one depends on whether you want rate certainty (amend duration) or flexibility (conditional top‑up). Below are two practical paths that procurement typically picks from. I attached a short spec sheet.

Option A — Conditional top‑up (recommended for this use case):
- Keep the current timeboxed POC.
- We enable an overflow bucket that bills PAYG for any tokens beyond the POC cap at a predefined overage rate (we can tier the rate for large surges).
- Minimum administrative change (no contract amendment required) — we’ll email an approval and enable the bucket.
- Good when you want to avoid changing scope but need emergency headroom.

Option B — Short duration addendum (rate certainty):
- Amendment adds X days with a small committed token slab.
- Lower per‑token unit price vs PAYG, but requires an addendum signature.
- Better if you expect sustained extra usage.

Dedicated burst window:
- We can provision a short dedicated pool (48–72 hours) and route only Quarry traffic to it. There is a runbook and a one‑time provisioning fee proportional to GPU-hours. We can cap the fee and usage.

I'll loop in Marissa for pricing and Connor for the ops/runbook. Attaching the one‑pager (Quarry_POCTopUp_Specs.pdf).

Next step: if procurement wants the PAYG overflow, reply with an approval email and we'll enable the bucket and share estimated overage rates and a provisional cap.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@quarrylabs.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC top-up/packaging options

Alicia — adding the pricing specifics here so procurement can make a call quickly.

If you choose Option A (conditional PAYG overflow):
- Overage rate: $0.0065 per token for the first 500k overflow tokens in the POC window, $0.0050 thereafter.
- Admin: email approval from an authorized Quarry signatory; no amendment required.
- Suggested soft cap: $2,000 to limit surprise bills (we can increase on request).
- Estimated provisioning lead: 2 business hours to enable bucket and alerts.

If you choose Option B (addendum to extend timebox):
- Example: 7‑day addendum for a 100k token slab at $0.004 per token (discounted), plus standard POC per‑day fees.
- Requires signed addendum (we can send a DocuSign).

Dedicated burst window pricing (48‑72hrs):
- Provisioning fee: $1,200 (covers GPU-hours reservation + routing changes).
- Optional SLA bump available for $300 extra.

I attached a draft addendum (license_addendum_draft.docx) for legal to review if you want Option B. If you want Option A, Alicia — please reply with the authorized approver's name and we will enable the bucket and set the soft cap.

—Marissa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@quarrylabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@quarrylabs.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC top-up/packaging options

Thanks — procurement here. A couple quick clarifications before we sign off: 1) If we enable the PAYG overflow, will overages be invoiced monthly or charged to card immediately? 2) Is the dedicated burst provisioning fee refundable if usage is below an agreed threshold (we often see spike windows that underutilize reserved capacity)? 3) Can you confirm the soft cap increase flow (exact approvals needed)?

We prefer monthly invoicing to centralize accounting. Also, can you send the DocuSign for Option B so our legal can pre‑review?

Ben Turner
Sourcing Manager, Quarry Labs
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@quarrylabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC top-up/packaging options

Ben — thanks, and good questions. Answers below and I’ve copied legal/ops for visibility.

1) Billing cadence for PAYG overflow: monthly invoicing is standard for POC customers; we’ll include any overflow usage on the next invoice. If you prefer immediate card charge, we can support that but it requires a billing profile update.

2) Dedicated burst provisioning fee: refundable up to 50% if actual GPU‑hour consumption is below 25% of the reserved window and you notify within 5 business days after the window closes. This is to cover scheduling costs but still share downside.

3) Soft cap increase: an email from an authorized approver (title/role acceptable) to pricing@redwood.com will increase the cap. For automated workflows we can accept the procurement mail alias if sent from a known domain. We’ll also add invoice alerts at 60/80/95% of the soft cap.

Action items:
- Ben: let us know preferred billing cadence (monthly invoice vs card).
- Alicia: confirm whether you want us to enable Option A (PAYG overflow) with a $2,000 soft cap today.
- If you want Option B, we’ll send DocuSign within the hour for legal review.

Attaching: Quarry_POCTopUp_Specs.pdf (same one as earlier) and draft addendum link (DocuSign).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
